agent_output.vulnerability: Kedro ShelveStore uses Python's shelve module, which is built on pickle, to persist session data. When reading a shelve file, shelve.open() with flag='r' deserializes the stored values using pickle.load(). If an attacker can place a malicious shelve file at the expected location (e.g., by controlling the session_id path or by planting a crafted file), the deserialization of the malicious pickle payload leads to arbitrary code execution (RCE). This is a classic CWE-502 (Deserialization of Untrusted Data) vulnerability.

agent_output.description: The GIT_RE regex in parse-url incorrectly parses git@host:path URLs, setting the resource to the entire 'git@host' string instead of just 'host'. This allows an attacker to craft a URL where the user field (git) is confused with the host, potentially leading to SSRF if the resource is used to make network requests. The vulnerability is in the fallback git-ssh parsing when parsePath fails.
